 Born to Stand Out Plans Shanghai Flagship Store Next Year
Medicube Now Sold at 1,500 Offline Locations in China
Cosmetics Exports to China Rebound for First Time in Five Years
 Business | Published 2026.11.17. 16:27:06 | By Kim Yeon-ha yeona@sedaily.com | Summary | Save A A A K-beauty brand Medicube's PDRN skincare line. Photo courtesy of APR Korean beauty brands that pulled out of China one after another during the THAAD dispute and the Covid-19 pandemic are moving back into the market. Skincare, color cosmetics and fragrance brands alike are expanding their China business by partnering with local distributors or setting up local units.
 Fragrance brand Born to Stand Out recently signed a partnership agreement with Chinese brand distributor Zhuying Group, according to the beauty industry on the 17th. Born to Stand Out plans to make a full-scale entry into China next year with the opening of a flagship store. Zhuying Group also handles Chinese distribution for Korean fashion brand Matin Kim. An official at Born to Stand Out said the company signed the deal with the local distributor to enter China in earnest next year, adding that the first store is expected to be in Shanghai.
 Earlier, APR's (278470) Medicube brand entered China's offline market for the first time last summer through a tie-up with a local distributor. Its main products are now stocked and sold at about 1,500 specialty beauty stores, including Wow Colour, Sanfu and Harmay. The Founders' Anua brand entered the Chinese market in August through Sephora China, and Dalba Global has set up a local unit there.
 Pharmaceutical companies are also moving into China through beauty. Humedix's aesthetic brand Elravie signed a strategic partnership agreement with a Chinese beauty company in July. Pharma Research, which operates Rejuran Cosmetic, signed a memorandum of understanding with a Chinese cosmetics company. An APR official said China is a market the company cannot give up, because success there has a strong influence on other Greater China markets as well as Southeast Asia.
 Cosmetics exports to China, which had declined for years, have indeed rebounded this year. Exports fell for four straight years from $4.87981 billion in 2021 to $2.01839 billion last year. But exports came to $1.77458 billion in the January-October period, up 2.7% from a year earlier. On an annual basis, they are expected to exceed last year's level.
 Still, some say it is too early to be optimistic, as the competitive landscape in China's beauty market has changed from the past. Patriotic buying favoring domestic brands continues, and local Chinese brands such as Proya are strengthening their product capabilities and cementing their position at home. The market share of Chinese domestic cosmetics brands rose to 57.4% last year from 52.8% in 2023, according to the China Association of Fragrance, Flavour and Cosmetic Industries.
